chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abu Dawud al-Mustaraqqq — whose name is Sulayman ibn Sufyan — who said:

Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: People rise from their beds in three types: a type for whom it is to his benefit and not against him, a type against whom it is and not to his benefit, and a type for whom it is neither beneficial nor harmful.
As for the type for whom it is to his benefit and not against him — he is the one who rises from his sleep, performs wudu, prays, and remembers God (Mighty and Majestic).

As for the type against whom it counts and not to his benefit — he is the one who does not cease to disobey God until he falls asleep; so that is against him and not to his benefit. As for the type for whom it is neither beneficial nor harmful — he is the one who does not cease sleeping until morning; so that is neither for him nor against him.

key_terms.أصناف: Types/categories — the tripartite moral division of people
key_terms.ذكر الله: Remembrance of God (dhikr) — key act of the pious waker
key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God indicating His greatness
key_terms.فرش: Beds/couches — the starting place of each person's nightly accounting
key_terms.معصية: Disobedience/sin — persistent neglect of God's commands

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about three types of people who wake from sleep?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) categorizes people who wake from sleep into three types based on how they spend the night: one who wakes, performs wudu, prays, and remembers God — this benefits him; one who spends the night in disobedience until sleep overtakes him — this is counted against him; and one who merely sleeps through until morning without worship or sin — with neither benefit nor harm recorded. This teaching was addressed to the Shia community of Imam al-Sadiq's era, reminding them that each waking moment is a moral and spiritual account with God, urging them toward the first category through prayer and dhikr.
